text:
Sophie: hey team — I'm debugging a model request that errored in prod. I have a trace id (trace-0a1b2c3d) and a req id (req-3f2a9b). Console trace shows spans but I can't find the raw log lines. where do you usually look?

Alex: start with the trace in Console -> Traces view. open the root span and check the 'attributes' panel for req_id or x-request-id header. often we surface a link called 'related logs' on that span. :mag_right:

Maria: if that link is missing, check the edge/ingress logs first — often the request id is stamped there. e.g.: ingress-nginx or envoy: `kubectl -n infra logs -l app=ingress-nginx --since=1h | grep req-3f2a9b`

Sophie: I did that, no hits in ingress. trace shows a proxy hop then our inference-pool service spans.

Alex: next: pod logs for the service. we have a small helper `rwdctl` (internal CLI) that can map trace -> logs. try: ```bash
# find logs by trace id (searches pod stdout + sidecar logs)
rwdctl logs --trace-id trace-0a1b2c3d --since 30m
```
If you don't have rwdctl, use stern: ```bash
stern inference-pool -n prod --since 30m | grep --line-buffered "req-3f2a9b"
```

Maria: for JSON structured logs you can also pipe to jq: ```bash
stern inference-pool -n prod --since 30m -o json | jq -c 'select(.req_id=="req-3f2a9b")'
```

observability-bot: automated hint — if Console trace spans lack a linked log, check span attribute `log_link.available=false` and ensure the service is emitting the `x-redwood-reqid` header or `req_id` field in structured logs. Docs: https://console.redwood.ai/docs/observability/log-correlation

Sophie: ok i'll try rwdctl. what about cases where request id is generated downstream (e.g., model worker) and not propagated?

Ryan: common pitfall. check for these places in order: 1) edge proxy (ingress/CDN), 2) api-gateway, 3) request router service, 4) model-worker pods. If the worker generates a new id, look for span tags: `generated_request_id` or `worker_req`. also grep for short uuids — sometimes we log only suffix. Example grep pattern: `grep -E "(req-3f2a9b|3f2a9b)"`

Alex: another trick: use the trace span timestamps to bound the search windows. if trace root start=2026-07-12T15:02:11Z, search +/- 30s around that in pod logs to reduce noise.

Sophie: ran rwdctl — it returned log pointers but no payload lines, only health-checks. Hm.

Maria: could be sampling or log-level. ensure the inference service logging level is INFO/DEBUG for that request. we throttle verbose logs in prod. you can temporarily enable debug for that deployment: `kubectl set env deploy/inference-pool LOG_LEVEL=debug -n prod` then reproduce. remember to revert. :warning:

Sophie: thanks. is there an on-call quick command to pull the full raw line (including headers) from the edge?

Alex: yes — for nginx with access logs enabled: ```bash
kubectl -n infra exec deploy/ingress-nginx -- cat /var/log/nginx/access.log | grep "req-3f2a9b" -n || true
```
If we use CloudFront/CF logs, open the S3 bucket via the console or run `aws s3 ls s3://redwood-prod-cf-logs/` and grep the decompressed entries.

observability-bot: tip — when you post a trace id, include the time window and the route (path + model) to speed lookup. Eg: `trace-0a1b2c3d | 2026-07-12T15:02:11Z | POST /v1/generate`

Sophie: thanks @observability-bot — trace + timestamp included. posted above.

Ryan: last fallback: if logs truly missing, enable request capture on one replica for a short window: `kubectl annotate deploy/inference-pool capture-headers=true --overwrite -n prod` (we have a small sidecar that dumps headers to stdout when annotated). use with care.

Sophie: OK doing that now. will report back. thanks all :pray:

Alex: ping me if you want me to run the stern commands from my machine (I have the right kubecontext).

Sophie: will do. updating ticket now. :white_check_mark:

Maria: FYI — I'll open a small follow-up to ensure the trace->log link is more visible in the Console for services that use the sidecar; low-effort UX win. :memo:
